speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to begin my assessment, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the pain radiate to your lower back or groin?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis / Painful Bladder Syndrome.

The clinical picture of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, significant frequency, nocturia, and dyspareunia in a 40-year-old female is highly characteristic of this condition. Would you like me to request a urinalysis to rule out infection or request images of the bladder via cystoscopy to confirm the diagnosis?
